- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly above recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast slightly below recent mean.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is volatile or mixed, add 2-3% upward bias to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– momentum (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to misalign with true direction; align forecast with sentiment trend, not just price history.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3-5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to anticipate rebound; add 5-10% upward bias if sentiment turns positive within next 5 days.
